title: Franchisee Is Not the Franchisor
scenario_text: Fernico Insurance is placing a liability policy and must identify the correct named insured after a claim exposes an entity mix-up. The brand "Chromel Fitness" operates 40 gyms. Two entities appear in the file: "Chromel Fitness Franchising LLC" (EIN 30-1120876, the franchisor that owns the trademark and licenses the brand) and "Redline Wellness LLC d/b/a Chromel Fitness" (EIN 82-9900321, an independent franchisee that owns and operates the specific gym at 88 Harbor St. where a member was injured). The franchise agreement makes clear the franchisee is an independent contractor, solely responsible for operating its location; the franchisor licenses only the brand and sets standards. The injured member's demand letter names "Chromel Fitness," the trade name, which both entities use in signage. An adjuster is about to tender the claim under the franchisor's master policy because the brand on the door is "Chromel Fitness" and the franchisor "obviously owns the brand." But the location is owned and operated by the franchisee Redline Wellness LLC, whose own commercial general liability policy names it as insured; the franchisor's policy covers the franchisor's own operations and brand, not the independent operations of each franchisee. Resolving which legal entity is the operator of the injury site, versus which merely owns the brand, determines the correct named insured and which carrier responds. The claim reserve must be posted this week against the correct carrier, and tendering to the wrong insurer would burn months before a coverage denial and leave the reserve mis-booked. The adjuster's file note already points at the franchisor's master policy because "Chromel Fitness" is the brand on every sign and letterhead, and the injured member's counsel is pressing for a fast coverage acknowledgment. The adjuster must trace the franchise agreement and the location's ownership before naming the responsible insured.
question: Which entity is the correct named insured responsible for the injury at 88 Harbor St.?
choices: Chromel Fitness Franchising LLC (EIN 30-1120876), the franchisor that owns the 'Chromel Fitness' brand on the signage.
Redline Wellness LLC d/b/a Chromel Fitness (EIN 82-9900321), the independent franchisee that owns and operates the gym where the injury occurred.
Both entities jointly, since sharing a brand name makes franchisor and franchisee the same insured.
Whichever entity the demand letter names, which is 'Chromel Fitness,' so the franchisor must respond.
